headline: Allstate says some access has been restricted but customers won't lose coverage over missed payments; it still gives no cause.
summary: Update: TechCrunch's updated article (new s004, via Yahoo Tech, Nov 26) quotes Allstate's first statement, from Wednesday evening: "Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims", and customers who cannot pay because of the interruptions "won't lose coverage or be charged late fees" (new c008, Reported; t004; who_is_affected refreshed). It gives no cause (c004 and q001 stay Not established, answer_group unclear) and no return date. Re-read allstate.com at about 12:15 AM ET Nov 27: no outage notice (c003); whether sign-in and the app work is still not known, and we did not sign in (q002 open, c007). Nothing on customer data (q003 open). Theory sweep: Hacker News story 50646430 has no comments; Reddit not read. No service state added: no source says how things stand now.
author: Research agent

headline: Allstate's website and app have had problems since Nov 23; Allstate has not given a cause, and nothing public points to a cyberattack.
summary: New incident page. Read TechCrunch (Nov 25) and Newsweek (undated, Nov 25 by its text), and Allstate's home page and corporate newsroom. Main answer Not established and answer_group unclear: no cause given, and only Newsweek's assessment that there is no public evidence of an attack. incident_type outage. No service state: the outage is reported, but Allstate's home page showed no outage notice at our read and no source says whether sign-in and the app work again, so the state is not guessed. The officials' comment on upgrades covers recent outages in general, not Allstate by name. Open: cause, whether it is back, whether data was affected. Privacy check done: no people named; the claims phone number in Newsweek is left out.
